Shanghai/Ningbo.waitLabel: SNH 4-7 days · NGB 3-5 days (as of 12 Aug)
Shanghai/Ningbo.note: Still backlog, not closure — Waigaoqiao, Yangshan and Ningbo-Zhoushan terminals have been fully open since 10-11 Aug. No source has published a berth-wait figure since SEKO's 12 Aug update, so the 3-7 day range is twelve days old and should be treated as indicative only. The congestion feed is no help either: Linerlytica has not published a snapshot since 16 Aug. New this run — Typhoon Saudel's forecast track now brings it to about 470 km from Shanghai/Ningbo within three days, against 596 km in five days a run ago. A 950 hPa, 85 kt system arriving on top of an unresolved queue is the main risk here.
Shanghai/Ningbo.source: SEKO Asia-Pacific Logistics Monitoring Center, 12 Aug 2026 10:30 HKT; JMA TC2621 forecast track, 24 Aug 06:45 JST

Xiamen.event: Tropical Storm Gaenari (Typhoon Saudel behind it)
Xiamen.note: Gaenari is directly over the port now — the JMA analysis position sits about 99 km away in the Taiwan Strait — but it is a weak system: 998 hPa, 35 kt, and Taiwan's CWA still rates it a tropical depression rather than a storm. No terminal suspension has been announced and SEKO reports the Xiamen office fully operational. The larger concern is Saudel, whose forecast track has shifted markedly closer: 158 km from Xiamen at the five-day point, against 452 km a run ago. Watch, not closed.
Xiamen.source: JMA TC2623 and TC2621 specifications, 24 Aug 06:45-07:10 JST; Taipei Times 23 Aug 2026; SEKO 12 Aug 2026

Haiphong.note: Third day of watch. Narra has stalled and looped in the Gulf of Tonkin roughly 114 km from the port instead of making landfall, dumping 130-250 mm on Quang Ninh, Lang Son and Haiphong. Sea-going permits have been suspended since 07:00 on 22 Aug and Hai Phong has more than 11,000 personnel deployed, but no source reports container terminal operations halted. Forecasts have Narra tracking back east then northeast, weakening to a depression around 25 Aug and reaching the Leizhou Peninsula on 26 Aug — so the flood and rain risk outlasts the wind risk here.
Haiphong.source: VietnamPlus and DTiNews, 22-23 Aug 2026; JMA TC2622 specifications, 24 Aug 06:55 JST

Shenzhen (Yantian).note: Operating normally as of the last published check, with ETB-7 gate rules active and 2-4 day vessel waits. Two systems sit inside the 600 km ring on forecast — Narra at about 521 km in three days and Saudel at about 378 km in five — but neither track puts a core over the port. Watch is precautionary. The 2-4 day wait figure is SEKO's from 12 Aug and has not been refreshed.
Shenzhen (Yantian).source: SEKO Asia-Pacific Logistics Monitoring Center, 12 Aug 2026 10:30 HKT; JMA TC2622 and TC2621 forecast tracks

remarks: Four systems remain active in the JMA feed, three of them near the China coast. No tracked port has changed status since the last run: Shanghai/Ningbo is still recovering, Xiamen, Haiphong and Shenzhen are still on watch, and no closure has been announced anywhere.

Saudel is the system that matters. It is the only true typhoon in the group at 950 hPa and 85 kt, and its forecast track has swung noticeably west since yesterday — 470 km from Shanghai/Ningbo in three days instead of 596 km in five, and 158 km from Xiamen instead of 452 km. If that trend holds another day or two, Shanghai/Ningbo goes from recovering to threatened while it is still carrying 1.89m TEU at anchorage.

Gaenari is the nearest system but the least alarming. It is sitting on Xiamen right now at 35 kt with JMA and Taiwan's CWA disagreeing over whether it is even a storm. Rain and short pilotage pauses are plausible; a closure is not indicated.

Narra has behaved awkwardly — stalling, looping and refusing to make landfall — which has turned a wind event into a rainfall event for Haiphong. Sea bans are in force but the container terminals have not stopped.

Two data gaps to flag honestly. SEKO has not updated its monitoring page since 12 Aug, so every berth-wait figure in this file is twelve days old and carried forward, not re-measured. And Linerlytica has published no congestion snapshot since 16 Aug, so congestion.json was left untouched this run — there was nothing new to merge.
